newsitem.title: CHINA: China delays bank ratio cut due to stocks - paper.
newsitem.headline: China delays bank ratio cut due to stocks - paper.

text.p: China has delayed a promised cut in bank reserve ratios partly due to its possible impact on the stock markets, the China Securities said on Thursday.
"Although a cut in the ratios is certain, it has not been implemented so far out of consideration of its impact on the securities markets," the newspaper said in a front-page editorial.
China's central People's Bank in July last year promised that bank reserve ratios would soon be cut.
But despite repeated market talk that the bank would announce the cut imminently, the reduction has yet to materialise.

"The central bank might be worried a bank reserve ratio cut will further boost speculative interest in the stock markets with more funds expected to be injected into the system on the cut," said an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage.

Under current rules, in force for the past eight years, banks and other finance institutions are required to put 13 percent of their deposits aside as state reserves and another five to seven percent for their own reserves.
The banks have urged the central bank to cut the reserve requirement as soon as possible, and in future to adjust the reserve ratio on a regular basis.

Industry sources have said the delay has also been caused by a resurgence in fixed asset investment from the second half of last year and that the central bank is worried a cut would further spur investment and consequently inflation.
